description.p: Skribisto helps you write anything, from a novel to course notes, without fighting formatting along the way. Organise a project in a binder tree of folders and items; the book's structure — Part, Chapter, Scene, Note — comes from the role you give each row, not from where it sits in the tree. Every writing row keeps its prose and its synopsis side by side.
Skribisto is not a word processor: a project exports to DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF, HTML, Markdown, Djot, LaTeX or plain text, so the final formatting happens in whichever program you prefer.

ul.li: Dual editor pane (prose and synopsis), with split panes and tabs
Read a whole chapter, part or book as one continuous document, or every synopsis at once
Corkboard, writing sessions, pace tracking and manuscript analysis
Search and replace across the project, trash with restore and undo, autosave and backups
Spell checking with downloadable dictionaries, light and dark themes, per-editor typography
Open several projects at once, each in its own window

ul.li: A project kept as a folder opens again after a file synchronisation tool or macOS respelled the accents in its file names, and saving into it edits those files in place instead of writing a second copy beside them

A project kept as a folder is the same project whether it is opened through its folder or through the project.skrib file inside it: it no longer opens a second time beside itself, and its backups are named after the folder and kept next to it rather than inside it
A backup file that ended up inside a folder project is left where it is instead of being copied into every later save and backup
The images of a folder project opened through its project.skrib file stay in the project’s own assets folder instead of being copied into the application’s data folder
A change made by an add-on on its own now counts as unsaved work, so closing, switching project or quitting asks about it instead of dropping it

Editing a pace, a milestone, a holiday, a text replacement rule, the punctuation settings or an image’s details now marks the project as unsaved, so those edits are saved and never dropped on close without asking
When a document’s text could not be handed to the save, Skribisto says which one and keeps the project marked unsaved instead of reporting it saved
Text typed while a closing save was still writing is saved too before the window closes, the project is switched or the application quits
The backup taken when closing waits for the final save, so it holds what was just written

A line of exported Djot that begins like a list item, a heading or a rule keeps the characters it starts with: a scene break written as 12. or (1), or a row of dashes, is no longer dropped from the exported file

Dragging several items at once when they sit at different levels, as the Corkboard's flat view lists them, now puts every one of them where you dropped it. Some of them used to land at a level computed from another item, which could leave the binder describing a different structure than the one on screen

A sentence cut or copied at the end of a paragraph no longer takes the paragraph break and the first letters of the next paragraph with it. This happened once something had been typed earlier in the document since the last deletion, and the stray text only showed up on paste
Bold, italic, Replace and turning paragraphs into a list land on the selected text again after typing elsewhere in the document, instead of the same number of characters too late
In a document holding a table, the caret can reach the last characters after the table again, and a selection to the end of the document includes them
